mainTopic: Whether רבי אליעזר holds that mixed blood does not truly blend (אין בילה): challenges from three ברייתות and from the משנה about mixed bloods.
overview: The גמרא keeps testing the view that, for רבי אליעזר, mixed blood does not truly blend (אין בילה). It brings three ברייתות about blood meant for above the red line that got mixed with blood meant for below it. Each time the answer is that the mixture is mostly upper blood, and the כהן places above more than the total amount of lower blood, so some upper blood surely went up. When a ברייתא says the lower placement counts, the גמרא explains that it counts only as שיריים, the leftover blood. In the third ברייתא, the words 'both count' are said to follow the רבנן alone, who hold יש בילה. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's cases of mixed one-placement and four-placement bloods. It answers them by saying the mixture held exactly one, or exactly four, placements' worth of each blood. The amud ends with a challenge from four-placement blood mixed with one-placement blood, which is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about upper and lower blood that got mixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It says that when blood meant for above the red line is mixed with blood meant for below, רבי אליעזר rules: place it above, and the lower placements count too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, a ברייתא says this openly: if blood meant to be placed above was mixed with blood meant to be placed below, רבי אליעזר says: he should place it above, and the lower placements count for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge by quoting a ברייתא. The next step explains why this ברייתא is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood goes above the red line on the מזבח, for example a חטאת. Other blood goes below it, for example an עולה. רבי אליעזר says that even when the two are mixed, placing the mixture both above and below is valid for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, explicitly
Blood meant to be placed above the red line
Blood meant to be placed below the red line
They count for him (he has done the מצוה)

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught explicitly:
Those placed above
that became mixed with those placed below
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He should place above
and the lower ones count for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another challenge to an earlier one ("and furthermore") against the view that רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that according to רבי אליעזר there is no full mixing (אין בילה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's ruling that both placements count seems to assume the blood is fully mixed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר about mixed upper and lower blood.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא is a problem if there is no full mixing
steps.stepSummary: If the blood does not truly mix, how can both placements count? Maybe the upper blood went below and the lower blood went above.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say there is no full mixing, why do the placements count for him? Maybe he put the upper blood below and the lower blood above!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no בילה, each drop stays what it was, either upper blood or lower blood. Then nothing guarantees that the right blood reached the right place. The priest may have done both placements with the wrong blood. Yet רבי אליעזר says both count.

keyTerms.meaning: Full mixing, so that every part of the mixture contains some of each
Why?
Perhaps
The upper ones (blood meant for above)

steps.confusionAlert: "אין בילה" does not mean the bloods are not mixed together in the cup. It means each drop keeps its own identity, so any one sprinkling might be only one kind.

phrases.english: And if you say there is no mixing,
why do they count for him?
Perhaps he placed the upper ones below
and the lower ones above!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין בִּילָּה, אַמַּאי עָלוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 1 challenges the view of אין בילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without full mixing, the right blood may never have reached the right place. So the ruling "עלו לו" would make no sense.

steps.title: The case has mostly upper blood, placed above in a measured amount
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a mixture that is mostly upper blood. The priest places above an amount equal to all the lower blood, plus a little more.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? One where most of the mixture is upper blood, and he places above an amount equal to the lower blood plus a bit more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a specific case in which the ruling works even without full mixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He places above more than the total amount of lower blood. So even in the worst case, at least some upper blood must have gone above. This keeps the ruling valid even if there is no בילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with?
A majority
A measure or amount
And a little more

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
For example, where there is a majority of upper ones,
and he places above
the amount of the lower ones, and more.
phrases.notes: Even if all the lower blood went up first, the "little more" has to be upper blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be talking about any mixture, which would require בילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about a mixture with mostly upper blood, placed above in an amount larger than all the lower blood. So upper blood surely reached the top.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says the lower placements count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the lower ones count. Under this answer, maybe all the lower blood went above, so how could the lower placement count?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches, "the lower ones count for him"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 3, using the words of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer explains why the upper placement is valid. But it is possible that all the lower blood was used up in the placement above. If so, the placement below might contain no lower blood at all. Yet the ברייתא says the lower placement counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches
The lower ones (blood meant for below)

phrases.english: But it teaches, "The lower ones count for him"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 3 (mostly upper blood, placed above in a measured amount).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer secures the upper placement only. The lower placement may contain no lower blood at all, against the ברייתא's words.

steps.title: The lower placement counts as leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: "Count for him" about the lower placement means it counts as the שיריים, the leftover blood of the upper offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It counts for the sake of the leftover blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading "the lower ones count" in a new way. It does not mean the lower offering's own placement was done; it means the blood counts as leftover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover blood (שיריים) of an offering like the חטאת is poured at the base of the מזבח, which is below. So blood placed below counts for that purpose. This avoids needing בילה.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of the leftover blood
Leftover blood, poured at the base of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר is explained without בילה. The case has mostly upper blood, placed above in an amount larger than all the lower blood. The lower placement counts only as שיריים.

phrases.english: For the sake of the remainder.
phrases.notes: He means the leftover blood of the upper offering, which goes at the bottom of the מזבח anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by reading the ברייתא's words differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "The lower ones count" seemed to mean the lower offering's own placement was done.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the lower placement counts as the שיריים of the upper offering.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא does not prove בילה according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: he already placed the mixture below
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. If the כהן placed the mixed blood below without asking, רבי אליעזר says he should go back and place it above, and the lower placements count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the כהן placed the mixed blood below and did not ask what to do, רבי אליעזר says he should go back and place it above, and the lower placements count for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to challenge the idea that the blood does not truly mix. This time the כהן already put the blood below the red line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood stays separate, maybe the upper blood was what he put below, so the lower placement should not count. Yet רבי אליעזר says the lower placement counts. This is the same problem as in step 2, now raised from a new case.

keyTerms.meaning: Consulted. He asked the חכמים before acting.
He should go back and place it again.
They count for him. The placement is valid.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he placed the mixture below the red line and did not consult —
phrases.notes: He went ahead without first asking the חכמים what to do with the mixed blood.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
He should go back and place it above,
and the lower placements count for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נָתַן לְמַטָּה וְלֹא נִמְלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that raises the same challenge as step 2, in a case where the כהן already placed the blood below.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that, for רבי אליעזר, mixed blood does not truly blend together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the blood stays separate, the lower placement might have been upper blood, so it should not count. The ברייתא says it does count.

steps.title: Same answer: the mixture is mostly upper blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers as before. The case is a mixture that is mostly upper blood, and the כהן places above an amount equal to all the lower blood plus a little more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the case is where most of the blood is upper blood. He places above an amount equal to all the lower blood, and a bit more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the new ברייתא the same way it answered in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is more upper blood than lower blood. So if he places above more than the total amount of lower blood, at least some upper blood surely went above. That makes the upper requirement certain without any need for the blood to blend.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too. The same explanation as before applies.
Most of the blood is upper blood.
The amount of the lower blood, and a little more.

phrases.english: Here too, it is a case where the majority is upper blood,
and he places above
the amount of the lower blood, and a bit more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by applying the answer from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a specific case (mostly upper blood).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about any mixture, which would require the blood to blend.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a mixture that is mostly upper blood, where placing a large enough amount above surely includes upper blood.

steps.title: But the lower placements are said to count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The ברייתא says the lower placements count, but under this answer all the lower blood may have gone above.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches: "The lower placements count for him"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave, the same way it did in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He places above an amount equal to all the lower blood. Maybe all of the real lower blood ended up above, and none was placed below. Then how can the ברייתא say the lower placement counts?

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches. The גמרא points to the wording of the source as a challenge.

phrases.english: But it teaches: "the lower placements count for him"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 7 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is mostly upper blood with a large amount placed above.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that answer, the lower blood may all have gone above, so the lower placement might not really be lower blood. Yet the ברייתא says it counts.

steps.title: It counts as leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: The lower placement counts only as the שיריים, the leftover blood of the upper offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It counts as the leftover blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers as it did in step 5: "counts for him" means it counts as שיריים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean the lower placement fulfills the מצוה of the lower offering. It means that pouring it out below is a proper way to handle the leftover blood of the upper offering. So the answer from step 7 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of the leftovers. It counts as the remaining blood of the offering.

phrases.english: For the sake of the leftovers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by reading "counts for him" as counting for שיריים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Counts for him" seemed to mean that the lower offering's own מצוה was done.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the blood placed below counts as the שיריים of the upper offering.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: he already placed the mixture above
steps.stepSummary: A third ברייתא: if the כהן placed the mixture above without asking, everyone agrees he goes back and places below, and both sets of placements count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he placed them above and did not ask, both the חכמים and רבי אליעזר agree that he should go back and place below, and both the upper and lower placements count for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא to challenge the view that the blood does not truly mix. Here the כהן placed the mixture above the line first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here even רבי אליעזר agrees that both placements count. If the blood stays separate, maybe the lower blood went above and the upper blood went below. Then neither placement should surely count.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those agree. Both sides of the debate admit this point.
These and those count for him. Both the upper and lower placements are valid.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he placed them above and did not consult —
these and those agree
phrases.notes: He means both the חכמים and רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: that he should go back and place it below,
and these and those count for him!
phrases.notes: Here "these and those" means the upper placements and the lower placements.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נְתָנָן לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא נִמְלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another ברייתא with the same challenge, now in a case where the כהן placed the blood above first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that, for רבי אליעזר, mixed blood does not truly blend together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the blood stays separate, the wrong blood may have gone to each place. Yet רבי אליעזר agrees that both placements count.

steps.title: Same answer again: mostly upper blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers once more: the case is mostly upper blood, and he placed above an amount equal to all the lower blood plus a little more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the case is where most of the blood is upper blood, and he placed above an amount equal to all the lower blood, and a bit more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third ברייתא with the same answer it used for the earlier ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he placed above more than the total amount of lower blood, some upper blood surely went above. So the upper placement counts without any need for the blood to blend. This answer secures only the upper placement; the next step points out that the ברייתא says both count.

keyTerms.meaning: He places (Aramaic).

steps.whatToRemember: All three ברייתות fit the view that the blood does not truly mix, through one idea. The mixture is mostly upper blood, and the כהן places above more than the total amount of lower blood. That guarantees the upper placement.

phrases.english: Here too, it is a case where the majority is upper blood,
and he placed above
the amount of the lower blood, and a bit more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 with the same answer used in steps 3 and 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a specific case (mostly upper blood).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both placements counting seemed to show that the blood must have blended together.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a mostly-upper mixture, placing above more than the total amount of lower blood surely includes upper blood. So the upper placement counts without any blending.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says both sets of placements count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the third ברייתא says 'these and those count for him,' which does not fit the answer just given.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches: 'These and those count for him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 11. The ברייתא says both the upper and the lower placements fully count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the כהן placed above an amount equal to all the lower blood plus a little more. If so, the lower blood may all have gone above, so how can the lower offering count? The ברייתא presents the result as something everyone agrees on, which would include רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: these and those (here: both offerings)
they count for him (the מצוה is done)
it teaches (in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it teaches: 'These and those count for him'!
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have this line. The square brackets show it belongs to the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ עָלוּ לוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is mostly upper blood and he placed above more than the lower blood's amount.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the upper blood is surely done, the lower offering should not count. Yet the ברייתא says both count, apparently with everyone's agreement.

steps.title: The 'everyone agrees' does not cover the last clause
steps.stepSummary: The agreement applies only to going back and placing below. The line 'these and those count' follows the רבנן alone, who hold יש בילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'these and those agree'? It says 'these and those count for him.' The last clause follows the רבנן, who say there is mixing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא carefully. 'Everyone agrees' and 'both count' are two separate statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees only that the כהן goes back and places below. The ending, that both offerings count, is the view of the רבנן alone. They hold יש בילה, so every drop contains both bloods, and both offerings are done. רבי אליעזר does not have to agree to that part.

keyTerms.meaning: agree
the last clause
we have come to the view of the רבנן
there is mixing (the blood blends evenly)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different 'these and those' appear here. 'These and those agree' means both groups of חכמים. 'These and those count' means both offerings.

phrases.english: Does it teach 'these and those agree'?!
phrases.notes: Here 'these and those' means the two sides of the argument, רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

phrases.english: It teaches: 'These and those count for him.'
In the last clause we have come to the רבנן,
who say there is mixing.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא: different clauses follow different views.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא, including 'both count,' was agreed upon by everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only going back to place below is agreed upon. 'Both count' is the view of the רבנן, who hold יש בילה.
steps.whatToRemember: All three ברייתות fit the view that, for רבי אליעזר, the blood does not truly mix. The mixture is mostly upper blood, and the כהן places above more than the total amount of lower blood. Where a ברייתא says the lower placement counts, it means as שיריים. In the third ברייתא, 'both count' is the view of the רבנן alone.

steps.title: The משנה: one-placement bloods mixed together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה: two bloods that each need one placement, once mixed, are given with one placement. Under אין בילה, that one placement might contain only one of the bloods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Bloods placed with one placement that were mixed with bloods placed with one placement are given with one placement. If you say there is no mixing, why is one placement enough? Perhaps he gives from this blood and not from that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, the משנה, to challenge the idea that רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bloods do not blend evenly, the one placement could be made up entirely of one offering's blood. Then the other offering would never be placed. Since the משנה says one placement is enough, it seems the bloods must blend.

keyTerms.meaning: one placement of blood on the מזבח
there is no mixing (the blood does not blend evenly)
perhaps

phrases.english: Come and hear: Those placed with one placement
that were mixed with those placed with one placement,
shall be placed with one placement.
And if you say there is no mixing,
why shall they be placed with one placement?
Perhaps he is giving from this one
and not giving from that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source, the משנה, against the same idea.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without even blending, a single placement might hold only one offering's blood. That would leave the other offering undone, yet the משנה treats one placement as enough.

steps.title: Exactly one placement's worth of each blood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a mixture of exactly one placement's amount of each blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where one placement's worth was mixed with one placement's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case so that both bloods surely go on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mixture holds only the amount of one placement from each blood, the כהן pours all of it. Then he has certainly placed blood from both offerings. No blending is needed, so אין בילה still works.

keyTerms.meaning: for example; it is a case where
one with one (one placement's amount of each)

phrases.english: For example, where one was mixed with one.
phrases.notes: He means just enough blood for one placement from each offering, and no extra.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of any amount of mixed blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mixture holds exactly one placement's amount of each blood, so both are surely placed.

steps.title: Four-placement bloods mixed together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה also says four-placement blood mixed with four-placement blood is given with four placements. Under אין בילה, maybe only one blood was used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four placements mixed with four placements!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the next case in the משנה as the same kind of challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four placements could all come from one offering's blood, leaving the other undone. So the same question returns, now with four placements instead of one.

keyTerms.meaning: blood that needs four placements

phrases.english: Four placements with four placements!
phrases.notes: Short for the משנה's case: these are placed with four placements, which seems to need even blending.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same challenge to the next case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Four placements might all come from one offering's blood, yet the משנה treats them as enough for both.

steps.title: Exactly four placements' worth of each blood
steps.stepSummary: Here too the case is a mixture of exactly four placements' amount from each blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is where four were mixed with four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before, now for four placements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mixture holds exactly four placements' worth of each blood, all of it is used. So both offerings surely reach the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: here too

phrases.english: Here too, where four were mixed with four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 the same way Step 15 answered Step 14.
steps.terutzMaskana: Exactly four placements' worth of each blood, so all of it is used.

steps.title: Four-placement blood mixed with one-placement blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the משנה's case of four-placement blood mixed with one-placement blood, where רבי אליעזר says to give four placements.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four placements mixed with one placement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more case from the משנה as a challenge. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case רבי אליעזר himself rules that four placements are given. Under אין בילה, those placements might contain only one offering's blood, leaving the other offering undone.

keyTerms.meaning: four-placement blood mixed with one-placement blood

phrases.english: Four placements with one placement!
phrases.notes: In this case of the משנה, רבי אליעזר says the mixture is placed with four placements.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the next case of the משנה after the previous two were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר rules that four placements suffice for both offerings, but without even blending one blood might never be placed.
